answer.rationale: C6 shows multi-year terms can cut unit cost, and C2 shows a prior primary-vendor switch delivered sharp, durable unit-cost savings with accurate invoicing and quick onboarding. The 18% mandate combined with the incumbent's refusal to reopen price this cycle is the binding constraint: renewal with no movement cannot satisfy it, and deferring (C5 pattern) does not address a hard budget target. A full primary switch with the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer is too aggressive in 14 days; the safer read is a small guarded test against the incumbent using a second-source component (C3 pattern: removing single-point-of-failure and de-risking supply) while running the price negotiation track in parallel. This conservatively harvests the cost-down evidence from C2 and C6 without betting the line on an unvalidated vendor at peak utilization.
